### 1970–1979

*   [April 19, 1970](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_sequence_of_April_17%E2%80%9319,_1970 "Tornado outbreak sequence of April 17–19, 1970") – A brief F1 tornado touched down south of [Thebes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thebes,_Illinois "Thebes, Illinois"), damaging several homes.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-StormData1970-90)
*   [June 14, 1970](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_sequence_of_June_10%E2%80%9316,_1970 "Tornado outbreak sequence of June 10–16, 1970") – A [multi-vortex tornado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiple-vortex_tornado "Multiple-vortex tornado") briefly inflicted F1 damage to [Mitchell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitchell,_Illinois "Mitchell, Illinois"), killing a dog. A camper was lofted over 300 feet in the air by the tornado.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-:2-91)
*   [June 16, 1970](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_sequence_of_June_10%E2%80%9316,_1970 "Tornado outbreak sequence of June 10–16, 1970") – An F2 tornado caused damage in [McLean County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLean_County,_Illinois "McLean County, Illinois"),[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-:2-91) and an F1 tornado caused minor damage to farms and outbuildings in [Colfax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colfax,_Illinois "Colfax, Illinois").[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-:2-91) Another F1 tornado briefly touched down in [Ford County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_County,_Illinois "Ford County, Illinois"), inflicting damage to outbuildings,[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-:2-91) and an F1 tornado caused minor damage to structures in [Clark County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clark_County,_Illinois "Clark County, Illinois").[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-:2-91)
*   [April 1, 1974](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_of_April_1%E2%80%932,_1974 "Tornado outbreak of April 1–2, 1974") – A relatively brief but strong F3 moved through [Lawrence County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_County,_Illinois "Lawrence County, Illinois"), damaging a [school bus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/School_bus "School bus") depot and multiple mobile homes.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Bridgeport-92)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Grazulis8-93)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-BridgeportNCEI-94)
*   [April 3, 1974](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tornadoes_in_the_1974_Super_Outbreak "List of tornadoes in the 1974 Super Outbreak") – A brief F0 tornado touched down in [Morris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morris,_Illinois "Morris, Illinois"), causing an unknown amount of damage. Another brief F0 tornado tracks through areas east of [Carlock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlock,_Illinois "Carlock, Illinois"), and an F1 tornado moved 16.7 miles through [Logan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logan_County,_Illinois "Logan County, Illinois") and [McLean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLean_County,_Illinois "McLean County, Illinois") counties. The tornado had a maximum width of 177 yards. A strong F3 tornado tore 18.2 miles across [Macon County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macon_County,_Illinois "Macon County, Illinois"), heavily damaging 110 homes and killing one person. A multi-vortex tornado destroyed structures on 8 farms near [Anchor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anchor,_Illinois "Anchor, Illinois") at F3 intensity, and an F1 tornado moved through land 8.2 miles east of [Taylorville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylorville,_Illinois "Taylorville, Illinois"). Another F1 tornado tracked across [Piatt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piatt_County,_Illinois "Piatt County, Illinois") and [Champaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champaign_County,_Illinois "Champaign County, Illinois") counties, while an F0 briefly touched down northwest of [Pierson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierson,_Illinois "Pierson, Illinois"). An F3 tornado touched down near [Tolono](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tolono,_Illinois "Tolono, Illinois"), destroying numerous structures and killing one person in [Philo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philo,_Illinois "Philo, Illinois"). An F3 tornado blew 3 trucks off of [Interstate 74](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_74 "Interstate 74") and damaged multiple structures near [Ogden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ogden,_Illinois "Ogden, Illinois"). An F2 tornado tracked 7.8 miles through areas north of [Bismarck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bismarck,_Illinois "Bismarck, Illinois"), damaging a high school. An F1 tornado moved 14.8 miles through [Coles County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coles_County,_Illinois "Coles County, Illinois"), causing an unknown amount of damage.
*   [July 23, 1975](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_Canton,_Illinois,_tornado "1975 Canton, Illinois, tornado") – 2 separate F3 tornadoes moved through [Canton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canton,_Illinois "Canton, Illinois"), the first causing an estimated $250,000 (1975 USD) in damages,[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Storm_Data-95)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Fulton-96) and the second killed 1+ people white causing $3 million (1975 USD) in damages.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Storm_Data-95)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Fulton-96) Both tornadoes were part of a related family that also produced an F1 tornado in Iowa.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Storm_Data-95)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Fulton-96)
*   March 20, 1976 – An F4 tornado moved 63 miles through the Central Illinois counties of [Piatt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piatt_County,_Illinois "Piatt County, Illinois"), [Champaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champaign_County,_Illinois "Champaign County, Illinois"), and [Vermillion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vermillion_County,_Illinois "Vermillion County, Illinois"). 10 injuries occurred in [Sadorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sadorus,_Illinois "Sadorus, Illinois") and [Ogden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ogden,_Illinois "Ogden, Illinois"), where members of the public described the tornado's [multiple-vortex structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiple-vortex_tornado "Multiple-vortex tornado").[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-97)
*   [June 13, 1976](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976_Lemont_tornado?action=edit&redlink=1 "1976 Lemont tornado (page does not exist)") – An F4 tornado tracked 8 miles over around one hour across [Cook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cook_County,_Illinois "Cook County, Illinois") and [DuPage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DuPage_County,_Illinois "DuPage County, Illinois") counties, mainly affecting [Lemont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lemont,_Illinois "Lemont, Illinois") and modern-day [Downers Grove, Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downers_Grove,_Illinois "Downers Grove, Illinois"). The tornado was noted for its erratic path, changing from a southeastern bearing to north to northwest, while being stationary at times. A roof of a reactor building at [Argonne National Laboratory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argonne_National_Laboratory "Argonne National Laboratory") was torn off. A total of 2 fatalities and 26 injuries occurred, alongside 13 million dollars (USD, 1976) of damage.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-98)

County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Clair_County,_Illinois "St. Clair County, Illinois"), damaging 32 homes and an elementary school.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-132) Another F1 tornado destroyed several structures and injured 2 people east of [Kenner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenner,_Illinois?action=edit&redlink=1 "Kenner, Illinois (page does not exist)").[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-133) trailer that they were occupying was flipped.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-134) A long-tracked and intense tornado moved across [Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_County,_Illinois "Union County, Illinois") and [Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson_County,_Illinois "Johnson County, Illinois") counties, destroying 75 homes in [Dongola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dongola,_Illinois "Dongola, Illinois") and killing one *   May 4, 2003 – An F1 tornado touched down in Kentucky, before crossing the state line into [Massac County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massac_County,_Illinois "Massac County, Illinois"), downing power lines and damaging trailers.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-138) Twin tornadoes touched down in [Pope County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_County,_Illinois "Pope County, Illinois"), inflicting F1-leveled tree damage before crossing into Kentucky and lifting a short time later.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-139)[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-140)[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-141)

miles through [Monroe County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monroe_County,_Illinois "Monroe County, Illinois"), uprooting trees and damaging a home.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-142) Another F1 tornado moved through areas southeast of [Red Bud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Bud,_Illinois "Red Bud, Illinois"), heavily damaging a home and destroying multiple trees.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-143) A storm chaser reported a brief F0 tornado in ### 2010–2019

*   [November 17, 2013](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Washington,_Illinois_tornado "2013 Washington, Illinois tornado") – An unusual powerful EF4 tornado moved through [Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_Illinois "Washington, Illinois") and several farmsteads in rural central Illinois, in the county of [Tazewell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tazewell_County,_Illinois "Tazewell County, Illinois"). The tornado killed 3 and injured 125 others.
*   [April 9, 2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Rochelle%E2%80%93Fairdale_tornado "2015 Rochelle–Fairdale tornado") – A violent EF4 tornado moved through [Ogle County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ogle_County,_Illinois "Ogle County, Illinois"), directly impacting the communities of [Rochelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochelle,_Illinois "Rochelle, Illinois") and [Fairdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairdale,_Illinois "Fairdale, Illinois"), killing 2 and injuring 22 others. It was the strongest tornado to occur in northern Illinois in 25 years.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-RochelleFairdaleIlTornado.gov-158)

### 2020–present

*   [June 20, 2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Naperville%E2%80%93Woodridge_tornado "2021 Naperville–Woodridge tornado") – An EF3 tornado struck the [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_metropolitan_area "Chicago metropolitan area") suburbs of [Naperville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naperville "Naperville") and [Woodridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodridge,_Illinois "Woodridge, Illinois"), damaging hundreds of structures, downing thousands of trees, and injuring 11 people. Two EF0 tornadoes were also reported near [Romeoville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romeoville,_Illinois "Romeoville, Illinois") and [Addison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Addison,_Illinois "Addison, Illinois").[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-159)
*   [March 31 – April 1, 2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_of_March_31_%E2%80%93_April_1,_2023 "Tornado outbreak of March 31 – April 1, 2023") – An EF1 tornado struck the [Apollo Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_Theatre_(Belvidere,_Illinois) "Apollo Theatre (Belvidere, Illinois)") in [Belvidere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belvidere,_Illinois "Belvidere, Illinois"), causing [the collapse of the structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belvidere_Apollo_Theatre_collapse "Belvidere Apollo Theatre collapse") onto a concert with 260 onsite. 40 were injured and 1 died.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-160)[An EF3 tornado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Robinson%E2%80%93Sullivan_tornado "2023 Robinson–Sullivan tornado") would produce EF3 damage in Illinois before crossing state lines into Indiana, where three would die.
*   [August 5, 2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_sequence_of_August_4%E2%80%938,_2023 "Tornado outbreak sequence of August 4–8, 2023") – A relatively brief EF2 tornado tracked 2.87 miles through areas near [Marcelline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcelline,_Illinois "Marcelline, Illinois"), damaging numerous homes and downing power lines.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-161) A tornado briefly inflicted EF0-leveled damage in [Jackson County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson_County,_Illinois "Jackson County, Illinois"),[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-162) and another EF0 was observed in [Jasper County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jasper_County,_Illinois "Jasper County, Illinois").[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-163)
*   [August 6, 2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_sequence_of_August_4%E2%80%938,_2023 "Tornado outbreak sequence of August 4–8, 2023") – A multi-vortex EFU tornado moved 8 miles through [Hancock County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hancock_County,_Illinois "Hancock County, Illinois"), causing no damage,[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-164) while a strong EF2 tornado damaged several homes north of [Pawnee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pawnee,_Illinois "Pawnee, Illinois").[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-165)[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-166)
*   [March 10, 2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_of_March_10%E2%80%9312,_2026 "Tornado outbreak of March 10–12, 2026") - A large and long tracked EF3 tornado touchdown in [Kankakee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kankakee,_Illinois "Kankakee, Illinois"). This tornado caused significant damage in [Aroma Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aroma_Park,_Illinois "Aroma Park, Illinois") and various other areas. This tornado tracked into Indiana before lifting. This tornado killed 3 people. This supercell produced multiple other tornadoes and giant hail.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-167)[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-168)

List of tornadoes in the U.S. state of Illinois

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a2/Mattoon_Illinois_tornado_damage2.jpg/250px-Mattoon_Illinois_tornado_damage2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mattoon_Illinois_tornado_damage2.jpg)

Tornado damage caused by a tornado that occurred in the [tornado outbreak sequence of May 25 – June 1, 1917](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_sequence_of_May_25_%E2%80%93_June_1,_1917 "Tornado outbreak sequence of May 25 – June 1, 1917").

[Tornadoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado "Tornado") in the U.S. state of [Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois "Illinois") are common, with 3,214 tornadoes occurring within state boundaries since 1950. These tornadoes have collectively resulted in 235 deaths.[_[improper synthesis?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:No\_original\_research#Synthesis\_of\_published\_material "Wikipedia:No original research")_]

## Climatology

Main article: [Climate of Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_of_Illinois "Climate of Illinois")

Illinois' climate is relatively average, and is only ideal for the formation of tornadoes in certain parts of the year, especially February, March and May. Warm air from the Southern United States can reach up into the [Southern Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Illinois "Southern Illinois"), resulting in tornadic storms. Illinois' proximity to [Lake Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Michigan "Lake Michigan") also results in cold air moving toward the Ohio Valley, creating the "hot-cold" effect seen in the traditional Tornado Alley. Illinois has had large tornado outbreaks in the past, including the [tornado outbreak sequence of December 18–20, 1957](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_sequence_of_December_18%E2%80%9320,_1957 "Tornado outbreak sequence of December 18–20, 1957") and the [1967 Oak Lawn tornado outbreak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1967_Oak_Lawn_tornado_outbreak "1967 Oak Lawn tornado outbreak").

Illinois is vulnerable to tornadoes with an average of 35 occurring annually, which puts much of the state at around 5 tornadoes per 10,000 square miles (30,000 km 2) annually.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-1) Peak tornado activity occurs between February and May, but storms can and have produced tornadoes in the winter.

### Pre-1950

*   [April 18, 1880](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_of_April_1880 "Tornado outbreak of April 1880") – A violent F4 tornado tracked through [Winnebago County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winnebago_County,_Illinois "Winnebago County, Illinois"), destroying multiple farms and killing one person before crossing the state line into [Wisconsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wisconsin "Wisconsin"), where more damage to homes occurred.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-2) An F2 tornado hit [Lyndon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon,_Illinois "Lyndon, Illinois"), destroying farmsteads. An FU tornado destroyed multiple homes near [Greenville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenville,_Illinois "Greenville, Illinois").
*   [Tornado outbreak of April 24, 1880](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_of_April_24,_1880?action=edit&redlink=1 "Tornado outbreak of April 24, 1880 (page does not exist)") – One of only two F5-strength tornadoes to affect central or southeast Illinois. This tornado touched down 9 miles southwest of Taylorville, then moved northeast through Taylorville (Langley/Langleyville) before lifting northeast of Sharpsburg. Bodies of people and cattle were reportedly carried over a half-mile. 6 reported fatalities and 33 injuries.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-3)
*   [February 19, 1884](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enigma_tornado_outbreak "Enigma tornado outbreak") – An FU tornado struck [Caseyville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caseyville,_Illinois "Caseyville, Illinois"),[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-autogenerated1-4) and another FU tornado caused an unknown amount of damage in [Metropolis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolis,_Illinois "Metropolis, Illinois").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-autogenerated1-4)
*   [March 27, 1890](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_of_March_27,_1890 "Tornado outbreak of March 27, 1890") – A relatively destructive F2 tornado initially touched down in [Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri "Missouri") before crossing the state line into [Randolph County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randolph_County,_Illinois "Randolph County, Illinois"). No known injuries occurred. Another F2 tornado touched down in Missouri, crossing the state border into [Sunfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunfield,_Illinois "Sunfield, Illinois"), killing 3 people. An F2 tornado killed one person in [Centreville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centreville,_Illinois "Centreville, Illinois"). A violent F4 tornado touched down in Missouri before moving into [Jackson County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson_County,_Illinois "Jackson County, Illinois"), killing 7 people and destroying multiple structures.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrazulis1984A-11-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrazulis1993648%E2%80%93649-6) An F2 tornado also tracked through areas south of [McClure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McClure,_Illinois "McClure, Illinois").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrazulis1993649-7) Another F4 tornado also touched down in Missouri, before tracking through [Alexander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_County,_Illinois "Alexander County, Illinois"), [Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_County,_Illinois "Union County, Illinois"), [Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson_County,_Illinois "Johnson County, Illinois") and [Williamson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williamson_County,_Illinois "Williamson County, Illinois") counties, killing 2 people along its path. A long-lived F3 killed 2 people in [Washington County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_County,_Illinois "Washington County, Illinois"), and an F4 tornado moved through [Massac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massac_County,_Illinois "Massac County, Illinois") and [Pope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_County,_Illinois "Pope County, Illinois") counties, killing 21 or more people and injuring over 200.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrazulis1993650-8) An F2 tornado hit [Olney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olney,_Illinois "Olney, Illinois"), damaging or destroying an estimated 33 homes and injuring 5.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrazulis1993650-8) Another F2 tornado tracked across [Wayne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_County,_Illinois "Wayne County, Illinois") and [Clay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clay_County,_Illinois "Clay County, Illinois") counties, injuring 10 people.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrazulis1993650-8) The final tornado to occur in Illinois during the outbreak was an F2 that tracked though [White County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_County,_Illinois "White County, Illinois"), killing one person and injuring 10 others.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrazulis1993650-8)
*   [May 25, 1896](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_sequence_of_May_1896#May_25_event "Tornado outbreak sequence of May 1896") – A violent and destructive F4 tornado moved through [Ogle County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ogle_County,_Illinois "Ogle County, Illinois"), destroying a church and killing 4 people.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Grazulis3-9) An F2 tornado touched down south of [Byron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Byron,_Illinois "Byron, Illinois"), destroying a farm and damaging trees.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Grazulis3-9) A long-tracked F3 tornado moved from [Davis Junction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davis_Junction,_Illinois "Davis Junction, Illinois") to [Irene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irene,_Illinois "Irene, Illinois"), killing 3 people and destroying 11 farms.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Grazulis3-9) A brief but destructive F3 tornado touched down in [Edison Park, Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edison_Park,_Chicago "Edison Park, Chicago"), damaging or destroying 36 buildings.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Grazulis3-9)
*   [May 27, 1896](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_sequence_of_May_1896#May_27_event "Tornado outbreak sequence of May 1896") – [A catastrophic and devastating F4 tornado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1896_St._Louis%E2%80%93East_St._Louis_tornado "1896 St. Louis–East St. Louis tornado") moved through [St. Louis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis "St. Louis") and [East St. Louis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_St._Louis,_Illinois "East St. Louis, Illinois"), killing over 255 people and injuring 1,000 or more. It is the third-deadliest tornado in United States history,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Mary_K._Dains_1896._pp_431-10) and caused over $10 million (1896 USD) in damages.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-normalized_damage-11) An extremely violent F4 tornado destroyed farms in [Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_County,_Illinois "Washington County, Illinois") and [Jefferson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jefferson_County,_Illinois "Jefferson County, Illinois") counties, killing 14 people.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Grazulis3-9) Another F4 tornado tracked through [St. Clair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Clair_County,_Illinois "St. Clair County, Illinois") and [Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinton_County,_Illinois "Clinton County, Illinois") counties, killing 24.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Grazulis3-9) The final tornado in Illinois of the outbreak moved through [Jefferson County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jefferson_County,_Illinois "Jefferson County, Illinois"), killing 3 people and damaging crops and other structures at EF3 intensity.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Grazulis3-9)
*   [April 29, 1909](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_of_April_29_%E2%80%93_May_1,_1909 "Tornado outbreak of April 29 – May 1, 1909") – A violent F4 tornado tore through [Saline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saline_County,_Illinois "Saline County, Illinois") and [Gallatin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gallatin_County,_Illinois "Gallatin County, Illinois") counties, killing five people and causing heavy damage in [Texas City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_City,_Illinois "Texas City, Illinois").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrazulis1993721-12) The tornado had a maximum width of 200 yards.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrazulis1993721-12)
*   [May 26, 1917](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_sequence_of_May_25_%E2%80%93_June_1,_1917#May_26_event "Tornado outbreak sequence of May 25 – June 1, 1917") – An FU tornado briefly touched down near [Pleasant Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleasant_Hill,_Illinois "Pleasant Hill, Illinois"), causing an unknown amount of damage but no injuries.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-MWR1-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Carey-14) An extremely violent high-end F4 tornado moved across Illinois, killing 101 people and injuring a further 638. The hardest-hit community was [Mattoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mattoon,_Illinois "Mattoon, Illinois"), where almost 500 buildings were destroyed.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-ClimIL-15) The tornado had maximum windspeeds of around 300 mph.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Burgess2002-16) A high-end F3 tornado tracked through [Coles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coles_County,_Illinois "Coles County, Illinois") and [Clark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clark_County,_Illinois "Clark County, Illinois") counties, destroying farm and injuring 15 people. Another F4 tornado touched down in [Will County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_County,_Illinois "Will County, Illinois") before crossing the state line into [Indiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana "Indiana"), killing 3 people along its 33-mile track.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-ClimIL-15) A brief FU tornado killed one person in [Randolph County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randolph_County,_Illinois "Randolph County, Illinois"),[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-ClimIL-15) and another FU tornado caused $80,000 (1917 USD) in damages to [Willisville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willisville,_Illinois "Willisville, Illinois").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-ClimIL-15) An FU tornado caused minimal damage in [Jackson County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson_County,_Illinois "Jackson County, Illinois").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-ClimIL-15)
*   [May 27, 1917](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_sequence_of_May_25_%E2%80%93_June_1,_1917#May_27_event "Tornado outbreak sequence of May 25 – June 1, 1917") – A destructive F3 tornado touched down in Missouri, before crossing into [Randolph County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randolph_County,_Illinois "Randolph County, Illinois"). One person was killed near [Chester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chester,_Illinois "Chester, Illinois").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-ClimIL-15)
*   [May 30, 1917](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_sequence_of_May_25_%E2%80%93_June_1,_1917#May_30_event "Tornado outbreak sequence of May 25 – June 1, 1917") – Two separate tornadoes touched down in [Ste. Genevieve County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ste._Genevieve_County,_Missouri "Ste. Genevieve County, Missouri") in Missouri before crossing the state line into Randolph County, inflicting F2 and F3 damage to at least 10 structures.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-ClimIL-15)
*   [March 18, 1925](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tri-State_tornado_outbreak "Tri-State tornado outbreak") – An extremely destructive and incredibly deadly F5 tornado moved through three states, one being Illinois. The tornado killed 695, making it the deadliest tornado in United States history. It was particularly violent in [Williamson County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williamson_County,_Illinois "Williamson County, Illinois"), and 102 people were killed in [West Frankfort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Frankfort,_Illinois "West Frankfort, Illinois").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMason2011278-17)
*   [May 9, 1927](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_of_May_1927 "Tornado outbreak of May 1927") – An F3 tornado killed one person and injured 12 others in [Schuyler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schuyler_County,_Illinois "Schuyler County, Illinois") and [Fulton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Illinois "Fulton County, Illinois") counties.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Grazulis-18) An F2 tornado briefly touched down near [Eden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden,_Peoria_County,_Illinois "Eden, Peoria County, Illinois"), deroofing a farmhouse but caused no fatalities.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Grazulis-18) Another high-end F3 tornado tracked 45 miles across [Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_County,_Illinois "Christian County, Illinois") and [Macon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macon_County,_Illinois "Macon County, Illinois") counties, killing one person.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Grazulis-18) A short-lived F2 tornado destroyed several barns near [Owaneco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Owaneco,_Illinois "Owaneco, Illinois").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Grazulis-18) A destructive F3 tornado damaged homes and injured 21 people in [Williamson County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williamson_County,_Illinois "Williamson County, Illinois"),[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Grazulis-18) and an F2 tornado killed 2 people in [Massac County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massac_County,_Illinois "Massac County, Illinois").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Grazulis-18)
*   [September 29, 1927](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_of_September_29,_1927 "Tornado outbreak of September 29, 1927") – An F3 tornado moved through [East St. Louis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_St._Louis,_Illinois "East St. Louis, Illinois"), killing 79 people and injuring a further 550. Losses from the tornado totaled $53 million (1927 USD).[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrooksDoswell_III2001168%E2%80%9376-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-21) An F2 tornado deroofed a home south of [Morrisonville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morrisonville,_Illinois "Morrisonville, Illinois"),[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrazulis1993814-22) and a tornado inflicted F3 damage to structures in [Cowden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowden,_Illinois "Cowden, Illinois"), killing two people and causing $10,000 (1927 USD) in damages.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrazulis1993814-22) An F2 tornado destroyed and damaged several barns in [Edgar County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_County,_Illinois "Edgar County, Illinois"),[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrazulis1993814-22) and an FU tornado was reported in [Conlogue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conlogue,_Illinois?action=edit&redlink=1 "Conlogue, Illinois (page does not exist)").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEUSWB1927424-23)
*   [March 16, 1942](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_of_March_16%E2%80%9317,_1942 "Tornado outbreak of March 16–17, 1942") – A violent F4 tornado moved through [Piatt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piatt_County,_Illinois "Piatt County, Illinois"), [Champaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champaign_County,_Illinois "Champaign County, Illinois") and [Vermilion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vermilion_County,_Illinois "Vermilion County, Illinois") counties, destroying over 40 structures and killing 12 people.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrazulis1993897-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHolcomb1942-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-ILX-Lacon-26) An F2 tornado damaged 13 farmsteads in [Fulton County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulton_County,_Illinois "Fulton County, Illinois"),[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-ILX-Lacon-26) and another F2 tornado damaged 10 farmsteads in [Knox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knox_County,_Illinois "Knox County, Illinois") and [Peoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peoria_County,_Illinois "Peoria County, Illinois") counties.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-ILX-Lacon-26) A destructive F5 tornado killed 7 people in or around [Lacon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lacon,_Illinois "Lacon, Illinois"), and losses from the tornado totaled $600,000 (1942 USD). This tornado is the most recent F5 or EF5 tornado to hit [Central Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Illinois "Central Illinois"). An F2 tornado killed two people in [Lincoln County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logan_County,_Illinois "Logan County, Illinois"),[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrazulis1993898%E2%80%939-27)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-ILX-Lacon-26) and an FU tornado was reported west of [Findlay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Findlay,_Illinois "Findlay, Illinois").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-ILX-Lacon-26)
*   [April 12, 1945](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_of_April_12,_1945 "Tornado outbreak of April 12, 1945") – An F2 tornado tracked through portions of Missouri before crossing the state line into [Adams County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams_County,_Illinois "Adams County, Illinois"), causing $3 million (1945 USD) in damages.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Grazulis2-28) Another F2 tornado moved through [Hancock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hancock_County,_Illinois "Hancock County, Illinois") and [McDonough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McDonough_County,_Illinois "McDonough County, Illinois"), causing $200,000 (1945 USD) in damages but killing nobody.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Grazulis2-28) An F2 tornado hit [Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industry,_Illinois "Industry, Illinois"), causing minimal damage to structures.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Grazulis2-28) An F2 tornado hit Missouri, before dissipating shortly past the state line in [Quincy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quincy,_Illinois "Quincy, Illinois"). 11 people were injured, and the tornado caused $250,000 (1945 USD) in damages.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Grazulis2-28)

*   [April 7, 1954](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_sequence_of_April_5%E2%80%938,_1954 "Tornado outbreak sequence of April 5–8, 1954") – An F3+ tornado tracked through areas southwest of [Saunemin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saunemin,_Illinois "Saunemin, Illinois"),[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-NCEISaunemin-37) and an F3 tornado destroyed 38 homes and killed one person in [Kankakee County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kankakee_County,_Illinois "Kankakee County, Illinois").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-NCEICabery-38)
*   [May 26, 1955](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1955_Great_Plains_tornado_outbreak "1955 Great Plains tornado outbreak") – An F2 tornado briefly tracked through areas east of [Coatsburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coatsburg,_Illinois "Coatsburg, Illinois").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-:0-39) Another F2 touched down south of [Pekin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pekin,_Illinois "Pekin, Illinois"), causing minimal damage.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-:0-39) An F1 moved through [Burbank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burbank,_Illinois "Burbank, Illinois"), and a long-tracked tornado inflicted F1 damage to structures in [Kankakee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kankakee_County,_Illinois "Kankakee County, Illinois") and [Will](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_County,_Illinois "Will County, Illinois") counties.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-:0-39)

### 1970–1979

*   [April 19, 1970](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_sequence_of_April_17%E2%80%9319,_1970 "Tornado outbreak sequence of April 17–19, 1970") – A brief F1 tornado touched down south of [Thebes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thebes,_Illinois "Thebes, Illinois"), damaging several homes.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-StormData1970-90)
*   [June 14, 1970](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_sequence_of_June_10%E2%80%9316,_1970 "Tornado outbreak sequence of June 10–16, 1970") – A [multi-vortex tornado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiple-vortex_tornado "Multiple-vortex tornado") briefly inflicted F1 damage to [Mitchell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitchell,_Illinois "Mitchell, Illinois"), killing a dog. A camper was lofted over 300 feet in the air by the tornado.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-:2-91)
*   [June 16, 1970](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_sequence_of_June_10%E2%80%9316,_1970 "Tornado outbreak sequence of June 10–16, 1970") – An F2 tornado caused damage in [McLean County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLean_County,_Illinois "McLean County, Illinois"),[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-:2-91) and an F1 tornado caused minor damage to farms and outbuildings in [Colfax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colfax,_Illinois "Colfax, Illinois").[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-:2-91) Another F1 tornado briefly touched down in [Ford County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_County,_Illinois "Ford County, Illinois"), inflicting damage to outbuildings,[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-:2-91) and an F1 tornado caused minor damage to structures in [Clark County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clark_County,_Illinois "Clark County, Illinois").[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-:2-91)
*   [April 1, 1974](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_of_April_1%E2%80%932,_1974 "Tornado outbreak of April 1–2, 1974") – A relatively brief but strong F3 moved through [Lawrence County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_County,_Illinois "Lawrence County, Illinois"), damaging a [school bus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/School_bus "School bus") depot and multiple mobile homes.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Bridgeport-92)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Grazulis8-93)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-BridgeportNCEI-94)
*   [April 3, 1974](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tornadoes_in_the_1974_Super_Outbreak "List of tornadoes in the 1974 Super Outbreak") – A brief F0 tornado touched down in [Morris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morris,_Illinois "Morris, Illinois"), causing an unknown amount of damage. Another brief F0 tornado tracks through areas east of [Carlock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlock,_Illinois "Carlock, Illinois"), and an F1 tornado moved 16.7 miles through [Logan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logan_County,_Illinois "Logan County, Illinois") and [McLean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLean_County,_Illinois "McLean County, Illinois") counties. The tornado had a maximum width of 177 yards. A strong F3 tornado tore 18.2 miles across [Macon County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macon_County,_Illinois "Macon County, Illinois"), heavily damaging 110 homes and killing one person. A multi-vortex tornado destroyed structures on 8 farms near [Anchor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anchor,_Illinois "Anchor, Illinois") at F3 intensity, and an F1 tornado moved through land 8.2 miles east of [Taylorville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylorville,_Illinois "Taylorville, Illinois"). Another F1 tornado tracked across [Piatt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piatt_County,_Illinois "Piatt County, Illinois") and [Champaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champaign_County,_Illinois "Champaign County, Illinois") counties, while an F0 briefly touched down northwest of [Pierson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierson,_Illinois "Pierson, Illinois"). An F3 tornado touched down near [Tolono](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tolono,_Illinois "Tolono, Illinois"), destroying numerous structures and killing one person in [Philo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philo,_Illinois "Philo, Illinois"). An F3 tornado blew 3 trucks off of [Interstate 74](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_74 "Interstate 74") and damaged multiple structures near [Ogden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ogden,_Illinois "Ogden, Illinois"). An F2 tornado tracked 7.8 miles through areas north of [Bismarck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bismarck,_Illinois "Bismarck, Illinois"), damaging a high school. An F1 tornado moved 14.8 miles through [Coles County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coles_County,_Illinois "Coles County, Illinois"), causing an unknown amount of damage.
*   [July 23, 1975](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_Canton,_Illinois,_tornado "1975 Canton, Illinois, tornado") – 2 separate F3 tornadoes moved through [Canton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canton,_Illinois "Canton, Illinois"), the first causing an estimated $250,000 (1975 USD) in damages,[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Storm_Data-95)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Fulton-96) and the second killed 1+ people white causing $3 million (1975 USD) in damages.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Storm_Data-95)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Fulton-96) Both tornadoes were part of a related family that also produced an F1 tornado in Iowa.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Storm_Data-95)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-Fulton-96)
*   March 20, 1976 – An F4 tornado moved 63 miles through the Central Illinois counties of [Piatt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piatt_County,_Illinois "Piatt County, Illinois"), [Champaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champaign_County,_Illinois "Champaign County, Illinois"), and [Vermillion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vermillion_County,_Illinois "Vermillion County, Illinois"). 10 injuries occurred in [Sadorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sadorus,_Illinois "Sadorus, Illinois") and [Ogden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ogden,_Illinois "Ogden, Illinois"), where members of the public described the tornado's [multiple-vortex structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiple-vortex_tornado "Multiple-vortex tornado").[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-97)
*   [June 13, 1976](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976_Lemont_tornado?action=edit&redlink=1 "1976 Lemont tornado (page does not exist)") – An F4 tornado tracked 8 miles over around one hour across [Cook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cook_County,_Illinois "Cook County, Illinois") and [DuPage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DuPage_County,_Illinois "DuPage County, Illinois") counties, mainly affecting [Lemont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lemont,_Illinois "Lemont, Illinois") and modern-day [Downers Grove, Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downers_Grove,_Illinois "Downers Grove, Illinois"). The tornado was noted for its erratic path, changing from a southeastern bearing to north to northwest, while being stationary at times. A roof of a reactor building at [Argonne National Laboratory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argonne_National_Laboratory "Argonne National Laboratory") was torn off. A total of 2 fatalities and 26 injuries occurred, alongside 13 million dollars (USD, 1976) of damage.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-98)

### 1980–1989

*   [May 29, 1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marion,_Illinois,_tornado_outbreak "Marion, Illinois, tornado outbreak") – An F3 tornado tracked 10 miles through [Randolph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randolph_County,_Illinois "Randolph County, Illinois") and [Perry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perry_County,_Illinois "Perry County, Illinois") counties, destroying 4 homes and injuring 7. The tornado caused an estimated $300,000 in damages.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-May_1982-99)[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-100) A violent F4 tornado moved through [Williamson County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williamson_County,_Illinois "Williamson County, Illinois"), killing 10 people and injuring a further 181.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-May_1982-99)[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-101) The tornado left over 1,000 people homeless.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-pahreport-102) An F0 tornado briefly touched down in [Saline County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saline_County,_Illinois "Saline County, Illinois"), damaging a barn.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-May_1982-99)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-103) Another brief F0 tornado touched down northeast of [Carrier Mills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier_Mills,_Illinois "Carrier Mills, Illinois"), downing power lines.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-104)[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Illinois_tornadoes#cite_note-May_1982-99)
